Cloudflare's Code Mode introduces a different way for AI agents to interact with large API collections. Instead of exposing thousands of individual tool definitions, it provides a TypeScript interface that lets the model write code, chain API calls, and execute them inside a sandbox. In its 2,500-endpoint example, Cloudflare reports reducing tool-definition context from approximately 1.17 million tokens to around 1,000. Anthropic has also introduced Programmatic Tool Calling, while Block's Goose project explores code-based tool orchestration. In this video, I break down what this means for MCP and the future of AI agents. To the tech industry: Just because you build something, should you? I first came across “Emma,” Nuance Lab’s new AI model, after seeing it go viral on social media last week. In many of the comment sections, I saw people questioning the intentions of the lab that created it. Most notably, I saw some people raise concerns about the wellbeing of the AI, not because they believed it was conscious, but because they felt this specific depiction of AI would be likely to face racial abuse. The idea of witnessing something that looked like them being dehumanized was very unsettling. And after interacting with Emma myself (and seeing similar type models be release over the last couple of months), I just don’t see the value of AI being depicted as so human-like. Until there are far more regulations in place, the risk of societal disruption feels too high.  #ai #futureofai #techtok
